title: Traffic-tempered optimizer guardrails for latency SLOs and safe config apply
creator: Sophie Ramirez
description:
Problem: automated batching and prefix/KV caching recommendations can reduce unit cost but occasionally increase tail latency for latency-sensitive routes. We need an automation layer that applies optimization configs safely: enforce per-route latency/throughput guardrails, SLO-aware routing (route high-risk traffic to conservative variants), and fast anomaly detection + automated rollback.

Goal: Implement a set of runtime guardrails and a staged apply flow so optimization recommendations can be applied automatically by policy while keeping 99th percentile latency within configured SLOs and preserving throughput for heavy routes. This ticket builds the control-plane + runtime checks for traffic-tempered optimizer guardrails and implements the validation and rollback playbook.

Scope: config validation service, staged canary apply with traffic tempering, SLO enforcement limiter components, routing tie-ins for variant fallback, and anomaly detectors with automatic rollback triggers. Excludes UI for manual tuning (tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Can schedule an automated config apply that is gated by route-specific 99p latency and RPS limits
Runtime limiter enforces a per-route max concurrency/queue depth that prevents latency regressions under bursty traffic
SLO-aware router can divert up to X% (configurable) of traffic to a conservative model/variant during rollout
Anomaly detector surfaces latency/regression within 5 minutes and triggers an automatic rollback when configured thresholds are breached
End-to-end test coverage + chaos test verifying rollback on induced latency spike
Telemetry: dashboards for pre/post cost-per-token, latency percentiles, traffic split, and rollback events
design_decisions: Use a two-tier limiter: conservative static limits (per-route baseline) + adaptive soft limits driven by recent 99p latency and queue growth
Staged apply uses progressive traffic tempering: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> target over configured windows with minimum observation periods
SLO-aware routing will prefer a list of compatible variants ordered by worst-case latency bound; each variant annotated with cost and latency profile
Anomaly detector uses smoothed 99p latency over a sliding 3-minute window with an absolute + relative threshold to reduce false positives
Rollback escalation: immediate traffic reversion on critical breach, followed by a post-mortem job to collect traces and KV cache snapshots
implementation_notes: Config validation: reject batching/cache profiles that reduce per-request headroom below formula: headroom = target_slo_ms - (baseline_tail + safety_margin)
Limiter implementation will be colocated with request router for minimal hop latency; use token-bucket for throughput and an additional concurrency semaphore for queue depth
Routing: add a small routing metadata field (optimizer_flow_id) to requests so we can track which experiments saw regressions
Metrics to emit: optimizer.apply.attempt, optimizer.apply.stage, optimizer.rollback.reason, route.slo.99p_ms, route.rps, route.queue_depth
We'll reuse existing rollout runner (runtime-rollout-service) with a conservative default plan; extend API to accept 'temper_profile' with percentages and windows
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Dry-run — compute expected cost savings and run in shadow mode for 24h on representative traffic
Phase 1: Canary — apply to 0.1% of traffic for 30m, monitor SLOs and queue depth
Phase 2: Warm-up — increase to 1% for 1h if canary stable
Phase 3: Ramp — 5% -> 20% -> target over configurable windows, stop/rerollback on trigger
Phase 4: Full apply — commit to route config and record final telemetry
monitoring_queries: sql:SELECT minute_bucket, p90_latency, p99_latency FROM route_latency WHERE route='chat.generate' AND minute_bucket >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 minutes' ORDER BY minute_bucket DESC LIMIT 30
anomaly_detection_rules: Immediate critical: 99p latency > target_slo_ms + 150ms AND absolute increase > 30% -> instant rollback
Rapid degradation: sustained 99p > target_slo_ms + 80ms for 10 minutes -> pause rollout and revert to last stable stage
Throughput collapse: route.rps drops > 40% within 5 minutes while backend success rate unchanged -> alert + automated revert
Queue growth: queue_depth p95 increases > 3x baseline within 5 minutes -> throttle optimizer apply and route to conservative variant
rollback_playbook: 1) Auto rollback trigger fires: runtime-rollout-service reverts traffic split to previous stable variant
2) Emit optimizer.rollback.reason metric with details (threshold breached, metric snapshot id)
3) Create incident channel and post automated diagnostics: recent traces, profile snapshots, cache hit ratio, and affected endpoints
4) Run rollback verification: confirm p99 latency returns to baseline within observation window
5) If rollback fails, escalate to on-call SRE and disable optimizer autosuggest for the route
6) Post-mortem: include config diff, timeline of events, and recommended fix before reattempt
testing_plan: Unit tests for limiter decision logic (static + adaptive thresholds)
Integration tests: staged apply using test harness with synthetic traffic (burst, gradual increase, cold start)
Chaos test: inject artificial tail-latency in canary variant to validate auto-rollback path
Performance test: end-to-end cost savings measurement on recorded production traces
E2E: verify that SLO-aware router correctly diverts traffic and that telemetry tags propagate
open_questions: What is the default safety_margin we should apply to headroom calculation for new routes (proposal: 25ms)?
Should conservative variants be limited to model quantization-only changes, or allow smaller context windows as a safer fallback?
How aggressive should automatic retries be after rollback before marking the optimizer profile as failed?
Do we allow customers to opt-out of automated rollback for specific routes? (security/compliance customers may require manual approval)
